RESOLVED 2026-08-08: .venv rebuilt on Python 3.12.13 via uv, for Streamlit Cloud parity. All 16 deps install and import. The old 'py3.14 lacks pymupdf/psycopg2 wheels' warning was stale — they build fine on 3.14 too; the real reason for 3.12 is that Cloud does not offer 3.14.

RESOLVED 2026-08-08: Supabase project created, DATABASE_URL set, 12/12 tables created in Postgres and all 47 assertions re-run there with identical results. ADR-005 nullability and the 6 CheckConstraints confirmed via information_schema. Residual: connection pooling under Streamlit reruns is only lightly exercised, and a free Supabase project pauses after ~1 week idle, failing like a bad password.

RESOLVED 2026-08-08: private bucket `finsight-documents` created (public=False, verified) and core/storage/files.py runs on the Supabase backend via SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY. The anon key cannot write to a private bucket (403 RLS); service_role bypasses RLS and never reaches a browser because Streamlit is server-side. 11 live assertions pass. Residual: no orphan-object cleanup when a run is deleted.

Phase 1 added two things the plan's ER diagram omits: a `milestones` table (the diagram draws 11 tables while the plan text and models.py stub say 12; ContractRules.milestones and TimelineEntry.payment_type='milestone' both require it) and expected_timeline.source_clause_ref_id (declared by TimelineEntry in interfaces.md, missing from the diagram, needed so an anomaly can inherit its proving clause).

Phase 1's 47 verification assertions ran from a scratch script, not pytest — tests/ stays docstring-only until Phase 6 by plan. The verification is therefore not repeatable in CI. Phase 6 owns porting them.

Import PyMuPDF as `import pymupdf`, NOT `import fitz` — the fitz alias emits a DeprecationWarning on the installed version. implementation_plan.md and project docs say 'fitz'. Affects clause_locator.py (Phase 4/5) and pdf_renderer.py (Phase 7).

PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-08-08: Supabase created; DATABASE_URL / SUPABASE_URL / SUPABASE_KEY are set and working. LLM_API_KEY generated locally. Still unset: HF_TOKEN (needed Phase 3) and the tunnel URL (Phase 5, see #9). Colab/Kaggle/HuggingFace/Streamlit Cloud accounts unverified.

ADR-011: the product now depends on a live Colab/Kaggle session. Tunnel URL rotates on every restart, cold start is minutes, and a dead session takes the whole app down. Mitigations are the Kaggle backup, a pre-warmed data/cache/, and a recorded demo — none built yet.
Accounts needed are now Supabase, Colab, Kaggle, HuggingFace, Streamlit Cloud. Google AI Studio and Groq keys are NOT used. Created by hand; the config page is the only check.
Base Qwen 2.5 3B will extract worse than a frontier model did. That gap is what Phase 10 exists to close and Phase 11 measures — do not treat early Phase 5 quality as a failure.
app/components/column_mapper.py is the one component in the tree Phase 2 did not build. It confirms an LLM-proposed CSV mapping (ADR-010), which does not exist until Phase 4.
Anomaly row selection uses st.dataframe(selection_mode='single-row'), which streamlit AppTest cannot click. The drill-down was verified by injecting session_state; the widget itself is manual-only.
The clause viewer shows page number, verbatim quote and locate_method but no rendered PDF page — pdf_renderer.py is a Phase 7 stub and seeded documents use seed:// URLs with no bytes behind them.

Supabase's CDN ignores cache-control: re-uploading DIFFERENT bytes to the same object key returns the OLD content for up to an hour, and a deleted object stays readable. Verified (server-side size said 7 while download() returned the 3-byte original). Mitigated by content-addressed keys (<run_id>/<sha256[:12]>_<name>) so a key's bytes never change. NEVER build a bucket key by hand — use files.save_upload and the returned documents.storage_url.

No orphan cleanup in Storage: deleting a run removes its documents rows but leaves the objects. Content-addressing means every edited re-upload also leaves its predecessor. Fine at demo scale (1 GB free tier); sweep before deployment.

SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY must go into Streamlit Secrets at deploy time, never the repo. It bypasses all RLS and has full DB access. SUPABASE_KEY (anon) is currently unused — files.py uses service_role and the DB goes through SQLAlchemy, not PostgREST.
